question: A 32-year-old woman presents 6 weeks after witnessing a fatal road accident. She has persistent flashbacks, avoids vehicles, reports emotional detachment, and has not returned to work. She was initially managed with supportive counselling at your PHC. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate next step?

answers.text: Continue supportive counselling alone for another 4 weeks

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Symptoms persisting beyond 1 month meet PTSD criteria. Supportive counselling alone is insufficient — this patient requires specialist referral for trauma-focused CBT or EMDR, which have the strongest evidence base for PTSD.

Benzodiazepines are NOT recommended for PTSD. They do not target the underlying fear memory consolidation and may worsen long-term outcomes by impairing emotional processing. Avoid in PTSD management.

answers.text: Refer to a psychiatrist for specialist trauma-focused treatment

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. At 6 weeks, symptoms meeting PTSD criteria (>1 month duration) that have not responded to primary care interventions require specialist referral. Trauma-focused CBT and EMDR are first-line evidence-based treatments requiring specialist delivery.

answers.text: Prescribe sertraline and discharge with follow-up in 3 months

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: While SSRIs (sertraline, paroxetine) have evidence in PTSD, initiating an SSRI without specialist review for a 6-week PTSD case with functional impairment is insufficient. Specialist referral should accompany or precede pharmacotherapy initiation at this severity.

overallFeedback.feedback: Review PS8.1 referral criteria: PTSD persisting beyond 1 month, especially with occupational impairment and non-response to supportive care, requires specialist psychiatric referral. Benzodiazepines are contraindicated in PTSD.
Well done. PTSD symptoms beyond 1 month with functional impairment unresponsive to primary care support are a clear referral indication. Trauma-focused CBT and EMDR require specialist delivery.
